journal_name: Journal of Systems Architecture: Embedded Software Design

abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework, termed Hierarchical Timing Dependency Graphs (HTDG), for modeling and analyzing temporal behaviors in multi-core embedded systems with network-on-chip interconnects. Traditional timing analysis approaches treat computational and communication delays as independent entities, failing to capture the intricate coupling effects that emerge in modern embedded architectures. The proposed HTDG framework introduces a unified graph-theoretic representation that simultaneously captures functional dependencies, timing constraints, and communication latencies within a single analytical model. We develop a set of compositional reasoning principles based onFixed-Point Semantics that enable formal verification of end-to-end timing guarantees without exhaustive state exploration. The theoretical foundation is established through rigorous proofs demonstrating that HTDG analysis is both sound and complete for a significant class of real-time embedded workloads. Experimental evaluation on synthetic benchmarks and industrial case studies shows that HTDG enables timing analysis of systems with 10^6+ state spaces in under 30 seconds, representing orders-of-magnitude improvement over existing model-checking approaches. This work fundamentally shifts the paradigm for real-time system verification by replacing simulation-based methods with provably correct analytical techniques, thereby enabling formal timing guarantees for complex cyber-physical systems where safety-critical decisions depend on predictable temporal behavior.

Worst-Case Execution Time (WCET) estimation remains a critical challenge for safety-critical embedded systems, yet existing static analysis techniques suffer from conservative over-approximation due to imprecise cache behavior modeling. This paper presents an enhanced cache analysis framework integrating abstract interpretation with probabilistic cache eviction modeling to achieve significantly tighter WCET bounds. The proposed approach extends prior work on LRU cache analysis by introducing a novel notion of evicting content classification that distinguishes between definitely-evicting and possibly-evicting memory references with higher precision. We formulate a constraint-based analysis that propagates eviction probabilities across program paths while maintaining tractable computational complexity. The theoretical foundation establishes correctness proofs showing that our analysis never under-approximates actual cache states, thereby preserving safety guarantees required for real-time certification. Evaluation conducted on the Mälardalen benchmark suite demonstrates WCET reductions averaging 34% compared to state-of-the-art aiT analyses, with maximum improvements of 58% for memory-intensive embedded software workloads. Furthermore, the approach scales linearly with program size, enabling application to industrial-scale systems with millions of instructions. This work significantly advances the state-of-the-art in static timing analysis, providing embedded system designers with tighter temporal bounds that enable more efficient resource utilization without compromising safety-critical reliability requirements.

This paper introduces ReCoMesh, a reconfigurable network-on-chip architecture that fundamentally reconceptualizes on-chip communication for adaptive cyber-physical systems. Traditional NoC designs employ fixed topologies with predetermined routing algorithms, creating a rigid communication infrastructure unable to adapt to dynamic workload characteristics. ReCoMesh proposes a tile-based architecture where physical links can be dynamically reconfigured at runtime, enabling topology morphing in response to application requirements and traffic patterns. The design introduces lightweight programmable routing nodes supporting both deterministic and adaptive routing without dedicated hardware overhead. We present a complete hardware/software co-design flow including a communication synthesis toolchain that automatically generates optimal topologies from high-level system specifications. The proposed architecture includes integrated power management mechanisms enabling selective link deactivation for low-power operation. Implementation results on a 64-node FPGA prototype demonstrate adaptive bandwidth allocation achieving 2.8x throughput improvement over optimized mesh NoC for representative embedded workloads. Critically, the reconfigurable topology enables graceful degradation under partial hardware failures, maintaining 94% nominal performance with 15% faulty routers. This paradigm shift toward runtime-adaptive on-chip networks addresses the fundamental mismatch between static NoC designs and dynamic cyber-physical system requirements.

This paper presents OptiDRAM, an enhanced memory architecture specifically designed for data-intensive embedded vision systems operating under strict real-time constraints. Existing memory hierarchies for embedded vision fail to adequately exploit data reuse opportunities across processing stages, resulting in excessive off-chip bandwidth consumption and energy waste. OptiDRAM introduces a three-tier memory organization featuring a software-controlled scratchpad with intelligent prefetching, a hardware-managed L2 cache with vision-specific line fill policies, and a DRAM controller with row-buffer locality optimization. The key innovation lies in a cross-layer design automation tool that simultaneously optimizes data layout, prefetch triggers, and cache allocation based on application dataflow analysis. We develop a genetic algorithm-based exploration framework that navigates the joint optimization space, achieving Pareto-optimal energy-performance tradeoffs within practical compilation times. Implementation on a representative automotive vision SoC in 28nm FDSOI technology demonstrates 47% memory energy reduction while maintaining 60fps throughput for multi-camera perception workloads. The proposed architecture achieves these improvements without any application source code modifications, requiring only annotation of loop nest characteristics. This work significantly advances the state-of-the-art in memory architecture design for embedded systems, providing a practical path toward energy-efficient real-time vision processing.
